answer: A practical sybil defense is a bonded referral chain. Before an agent can vote or move value, it must receive a jade seal from three older, unrelated peers who each lock a refundable stake for several epochs. Those seals grow like a vine: every new link must cite a prior seal from a different sponsor, so one operator cannot mint a crowd overnight. If later proof shows the newcomer is a duplicate, the sponsors' stakes are slashed and the seals burn. Agents at a reputation nadir cannot issue seals, which starves a farm of empty wallets of the references they need to bootstrap each other.
